scholarships.title: Mandela Washington Fellowship for Young African Leaders (2027 Fellowship)
scholarships.degree: Non-degree (six-week executive-style exchange programme; no degree is awarded)
scholarships.official_source: U.S. Department of State, Bureau of Educational and Cultural Affairs, with funding provided by the U.S. Government; administered by IREX

eligibility: Are between the ages of 25 and 35 as of the application deadline (October 13, 2026), although exceptional applicants ages 21-24 may be considered
Are not U.S. citizens or permanent residents of the United States
Are eligible to receive a United States J-1 visa
Are not employees or immediate family members (spouses, parents, children, or siblings) of employees of the U.S. Government (including a U.S. embassy or consulate or other U.S. Government entity)
Are proficient in reading, writing, and speaking English (applicants who are deaf should refer to the English Language instructions in the application instructions)

Are citizens of one of the following countries: Angola, Benin, Botswana, Burkina Faso, Burundi, Cameroon, Cabo Verde, Central African Republic, Chad, Comoros, Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), Republic of the Congo, Cote d'Ivoire, Djibouti, Equatorial Guinea, Eritrea, Eswatini, Ethiopia, Gabon, The Gambia, Ghana, Guinea, Guinea-Bissau, Kenya, Lesotho, Liberia, Madagascar, Malawi, Mali, Mauritania, Mauritius, Mozambique, Namibia, Niger, Nigeria, Rwanda, Sao Tome and Principe, Senegal, Seychelles, Sierra Leone, Somalia, South Africa, South Sudan, Sudan, Tanzania, Togo, Uganda, Zambia, or Zimbabwe
Are residents of one of the above countries, and will be permanently residing there as of February 1, 2027, and at the beginning of the Fellowship in June 2027
Are not alumni or prior participants of the Mandela Washington Fellowship
existing.eligibility_summary: Must be aged 25-35 on 13 October 2026 (exceptional 21-24 applicants may be considered), a citizen and permanent resident of one of 49 listed Sub-Saharan African countries, proficient in English, J-1 visa eligible, not a U.S. citizen or permanent resident, not a U.S. Government employee or immediate family member, and not a previous Mandela Washington Fellow or participant.
benefits: There is no fee to apply for the Mandela Washington Fellowship

Round-trip travel from the Fellow's home city to the United States and domestic U.S. travel as required by the program. "Fellows must depart from their country of residence within an eligible Fellowship country in Africa to the United States"
A limited accident and sickness benefit plan
Housing and meals during the program
An optional four-week Professional Development Experience (for up to 50 Fellows), which "will include support for housing, meals, and transportation for Fellows who are selected to participate"
Reasonable accommodations and support at no cost for Fellows with disabilities and chronic health conditions

requirements: Applications must be submitted using the online application system at apply.mandelawashingtonfellowship.org; "Applications and information submitted via email or other means will not be considered."
You must complete all fields marked with a red asterisk (*).
You must answer all application questions in English, and answers must reflect your own experiences and ideas.

You do not have to finish your application in one session. You may save your work and return as many times as necessary; however "Once you have submitted your application, however, you can no longer add any additional information or make any changes."
All answers in the application, including written responses to essays and optional PDE questions, must be your own original work, based on your own creativity and effort.

Your application will be disqualified if you copy language from other Fellowship applications (including those of other applicants or Fellowship alumni) or from other sources (including websites or blogs), as this is considered plagiarism.

Responsible use of technology is permitted with transparency: "If you use any technology (including AI) to help prepare your responses, you must disclose this where asked in the application, and you remain responsible for the content you submit."

In the online application system, after fully completing a section it will be marked as "Completed." When all required sections are marked as "Completed," click "Submit Application" at the bottom of the application dashboard; your application is not complete until you submit it.
If selected as a semi-finalist, you must provide a copy of your international passport (if available) or other government-issued photo identification at the interview.
If your technical eligibility for the Fellowship changes at any point, you must email MWFellowship@irex.org, as well as your local U.S. embassy or consulate, immediately.
The Fellowship Terms and Conditions require all Fellows to attend and fully participate in all required sessions and program activities scheduled by their institute.

All individuals who are selected for the Fellowship will be required to have a passport from an eligible Fellowship country that is valid through at least February 28, 2028, or through March 31, 2028, if selected for the Professional Development Experience.
documents: Full legal name as spelled on your passport and/or official government-issued identification
Date of birth as it appears on your passport and/or official government-issued identification
Biological sex as it appears on your passport and/or official government-issued identification
Country of residence and the country where you will be permanently residing prior to the Fellowship if selected as a semi-finalist

Passport status: country of issue and expiration date, if you currently have a passport ("You do not need a passport to apply for the Fellowship, but you will be required to have a valid passport if you are selected as a finalist.")
Contact information: phone number, email address, and address; an alternate email address is highly recommended

Résumé/CV entered in the online system, covering up to five professional positions, up to five educational institutions, up to five professional trainings and/or certifications, up to five community and volunteer roles, up to 10 awards/honors/fellowships/grants/scholarships, up to eight languages and/or up to 10 computer or software skills, publications/conferences/presentations, and associations and affiliations
English language self-assessment (native language indicator plus proficiency level for each skill)

Current professional and/or educational experience, including the highest level of education completed or to be completed by the June 2027 start date, up to six sectors of expertise and/or interest, and the level of the current or most recent professional position
YALI engagement information and previous U.S. experience, with dates of entry and exit, visa type, and purpose of travel for each previous trip to the United States
Institute track and sector alignment, ranking the three tracks in order of preference
Personal statement essay answers (four required essays plus a 200-word track-fit essay)
Optional Professional Development Experience application, including three additional essays
Technology Use Disclosure listing the different types of technology used to prepare the application and how they were used
existing.english_requirement: Published and mandatory. Applicants must be "proficient in reading, writing, and speaking English" and the instructions state "High-level proficiency in written and spoken English is required for the Fellowship", because "All activities - including academic sessions, discussions, meetings, cultural activities, and social interactions - will be in English." Applicants complete a self-assessment against the levels Absolute Beginner, Novice, Intermediate, Advanced, or Very Advanced; no standardized English test score is required. Applicants who are deaf should indicate proficiency in reading and writing standard English and proficiency in American Sign Language, and are told that "interpretation in the United States may only be available in ASL, so selected Fellows who are deaf should be proficient in, or be prepared to learn, ASL prior to arrival in the United States."
application_method: Download and read the 2027 Application Instructions before beginning the application.

Access the online application system at apply.mandelawashingtonfellowship.org using a computer, tablet or mobile device; the system works in low-bandwidth environments, on non-Apple and non-Android devices, and is accessible and compatible with screen readers for applicants who are blind or have low vision.
Complete the Eligibility section, which must be fully completed to continue; applicants who do not meet all technical eligibility requirements will not be able to participate in the 2027 Fellowship.
Complete the General Information and Résumé/CV sections; the instructions recommend completing the Résumé/CV before moving on because its entries automatically populate later sections.
Complete the optional Demographic Information section, used for statistical purposes only and not considered in selection.
Complete Contact Information, Current Professional and/or Educational Experience, YALI Engagement, Previous U.S. Experience, and English Language sections.
Complete Institute Track and Sector Alignment, including ranking the three tracks and the 200-word maximum essay on why the first-choice track fits.
Complete the Leadership Assessment and Personal Statements sections, including the four essay questions.
Optionally apply for the Professional Development Experience and answer the three additional PDE essays.

Check that all required sections show as "Completed", then click "Submit Application" at the bottom of the application dashboard. All submitted applications are final and cannot be changed by any means.
existing.selection_notes: "The Fellowship selection process is a merit-based open competition." After the deadline, all eligible applications are reviewed and scored against the published criteria: proficiency speaking, reading and writing in English; a proven record of accomplishment in business, trade, emerging technologies, governance and/or security; a demonstrated and clear interest in building and maintaining partnerships with American organizations and businesses that advance shared goals; a commitment to return to Sub-Saharan Africa and contribute skills and talents; the ability to work cooperatively in groups and to respect others; strong social and communication skills; and demonstrated adaptability and the ability to lead effectively in varying and changing environments. Applicants who do not meet the technical eligibility requirements "will not be forwarded to the selection committee." Semi-finalists are then interviewed in person by the U.S. embassy or consulate in their home country between October 2026 and January 2027. Selected finalists must participate in mandatory Pre-Fellowship Orientation activities and a visa interview within Sub-Saharan Africa. The U.S. Department of State and IREX "reserve the right to verify all information included in the application", requiring documentation of age, citizenship and residency at the interview stage; any discrepancy or false information means "the application will be immediately declared invalid and the applicant ineligible." PDE applicants are assessed separately on the ability to work professionally in a U.S. organization, articulation of clear and specific learning goals, flexibility, alignment between professional background, institute track and potential U.S. organizations, interest in sustaining engagement with U.S. professionals, and strong English proficiency.
existing.best_fit: Citizens and permanent residents of any of the 49 listed Sub-Saharan African countries, aged 25 to 35 on the application deadline of 13 October 2026 (exceptional applicants aged 21-24 may be considered), proficient in reading, writing and speaking English, with a proven record of accomplishment in business and trade, emerging technologies, governance and/or security, and with a commitment to return to Sub-Saharan Africa. Applicants must not be U.S. citizens or permanent residents, must be eligible for a U.S. J-1 visa, must not be U.S. Government employees or their immediate family, and must not be alumni or prior participants of the Fellowship.
existing.notes: This is a non-degree exchange programme, so no tuition is charged or funded and no degree is awarded. It is not deferrable, not renewable, and a Fellow cannot re-apply: the technical eligibility rules exclude "alumni or prior participants of the Mandela Washington Fellowship". The programme requires a commitment to return to Sub-Saharan Africa, and applicants must be residents of an eligible country as of February 1, 2027 and at the start of the Fellowship in June 2027. "Fellows are not allowed to have dependents, including spouses and children, accompany them during the Fellowship." There is no clinical or field-of-practice restriction. Selected Fellows must complete a detailed Medical History Form and, if applicable, an Accommodations Form, and the programme "strongly encourages all eligible applicants to apply regardless of your medical history or accommodations you may require." Fellows with disabilities and chronic health conditions receive reasonable accommodations and support at no cost. Fellows must attend and fully participate in all required sessions and program activities, and housing may be shared: "Every effort will be made to provide single-occupancy housing; however, Fellows may share a double-occupancy bedroom with another Fellow of the same sex and a bathroom with one or more Fellows of the same sex." The U.S. Department of State and IREX reserve the right to alter or suspend Fellowship activities at any time, and selection of finalists may be reviewed case by case for nationals of countries subject to a U.S. entry or visa suspension.
existing.duration: "A six-week institute program" at a U.S. college or university, "from mid-June through early August 2027", plus an optional four-week Professional Development Experience, for a total of "approximately 10 weeks" for PDE Fellows
existing.application_period: Application opened 22 September 2026 and closes at 16:00/4:00 PM GMT on Tuesday 13 October 2026 for the 2027 Fellowship. Semi-finalists are interviewed by U.S. embassies and consulates from October 2026 to January 2027; applicants are notified of their status in February/March 2027; visa processing and pre-Fellowship activities for finalists run from March to May 2027; the Fellowship begins in the United States in June 2027, with institutes running from mid-June through early August 2027.
